fact_en: A scanning electron microscope bounces an electron beam off the surface of a sample to create a three-dimensional image of its outside.
fact_bis: Ang scanning electron microscope nagpapabukal sa electron beam sa surface sa usa ka sample aron makahimo ug three-dimensional nga imahe sa gawas niini.

findings.note: EN: SEM "bounces an electron beam off the surface of a sample". BIS: "NAGPAPABUKAL sa electron beam sa surface" — same bukal = TO BOIL false friend (and in a Tagalog-shaped nagpapa- form that is not Cebuano morphology). The mechanism that distinguishes SEM from the TEM card (beam bounces off the surface vs passes through) is replaced by a nonsense claim that the beam is boiled, and the card never corrects it; only "surface" and "imahe sa gawas" survive.

fact_en: The thermosphere contains the ionosphere, a region of charged gas particles that bounces radio waves and creates glowing auroras near the poles.
fact_bis: Ang thermosphere adunay ionosphere, usa ka bahin sa charged gas particles nga nagpabukal sa radio waves ug naghimo sa nagdan-ag nga auroras duol sa mga polo.

findings.note: EN: ionosphere "bounces radio waves". BIS: "charged gas particles nga NAGPABUKAL sa radio waves" — bukal = TO BOIL in Cebuano (pabukal = to make boil); it never means bounce/reflect (mobalik, mabanda, mo-reflect). A Cebuano-only child is told the ionosphere BOILS radio waves, which is false, and nothing else in the card restores the reflection fact — the rest of the card only covers auroras.

fact_en: Dragonflies use their wings to fly and chase other flying insects, which they catch and eat.
fact_bis: Gigamit sa mga tambubuyog ang ilang mga pako sa paglupad ug paggukod sa uban pang naglupad nga mga insekto, nga ilang gidakop ug gikaon.

findings.note: Title and body both name a bee, not a dragonfly. 'Dragonfly Wings' -> 'Mga Pako sa Tambubuyog'; body: 'Gigamit sa mga tambubuyog ang ilang mga pako... paggukod sa uban pang naglupad nga mga insekto, nga ilang gidakop ug gikaon.' Cebuano tambubuyog = bumblebee/large bee; dragonfly is alindahaw (or tutubi). Nothing in the card corrects it and 'tambubuyog' is even the emph term, so a child reading only the Cebuano learns that bees hunt, catch and eat other flying insects - false, and the actual subject (dragonfly) is never delivered. Every other dragonfly card in this sweep uses alindahaw/tutubi (ffct-07591 'Ang alindahaw usa ka insekto nga adunay unom ka tiil ug upat ka pako', ffct-09640, ffct-12024, ffct-04274, ffct-05558...); tambubuyog appears nowhere else in the corpus.

fact_en: When the Sun is high in the sky, its rays strike the ground at a steep angle, concentrating solar energy on a smaller area and causing more heating.
fact_bis: Kung taas na ang adlaw sa langit, titipid ang anggulo sa iyang silaw sa yuta, busa ang solar energy mag-concentrate sa mas gamay nga lugar ug mas moinit.

findings.note: bis body: "titipid ang anggulo sa iyang silaw sa yuta" for EN "its rays strike the ground at a steep angle", and "titipid" is also the emph_bis highlighted term. Cebuano for steep is tarik/matarik; titipid is the Tagalog verb form of tipid (to economize/be thrifty) and means nothing like "steep" in Cebuano. Worse, a child reads it as the angle being reduced/small, which is the opposite of steep and contradicts the paired card dcard-09592 (low angle = energy spread, cooler). Corpus check: all 369 other "titipid" hits are Tagalog "pagtitipid ng kuryente" energy-saving text, and this same card's tl emphasis is the correct "matarik".

fact_en: Before an earthquake, follow your local disaster readiness plan so your family knows the safe spots, emergency kits, and meeting places ahead of time.
fact_bis: Sa dili pa molinog, sunda ang local disaster readiness plan aron mahibalo na sa imong pamilya ang mga luwas nga lugar, emergency kit, ug tigumanan daan.

findings.note: title_bis "Sa Dili Pa Mout-og" for "Before the Shaking". Cebuano for earthquake shaking is uyog/kurog (the very next card, dcard-09617, correctly uses "Samtang mouyog", and this card's own body says "Sa dili pa molinog"). "Ut-og" is not a shaking word in Cebuano — utog means sexual arousal/erection, so the card heading a grade-5 child sees reads as "Before Getting an Erection". Corpus check: "Mout-og" appears nowhere else in the corpus, and this card's tl title is the correct "Bago ang Pagyanig", so the bis title is the lone outlier.

fact_en: Nitrogen fixation is the process in which nitrogen gas from the air is converted into nitrates or ammonia, often by bacteria or by lightning during thunderstorms.
fact_bis: Ang nitrogen fixation mao ang proseso diin ang nitrogen gas sa hangin himoon nga nitrates o ammonia, kasagaran sa bacteria o sa kilat panahon sa bagyo.

findings.note: title_bis "Pag-ayo sa Nitrogen" for "Fixing Nitrogen". Pag-ayo in Cebuano means repairing/healing/improving — it names a different action than nitrogen fixation (converting N2 gas into nitrates/ammonia). The card's own body keeps the correct term ("Ang nitrogen fixation mao ang proseso diin ang nitrogen gas sa hangin himoon nga nitrates o ammonia"), so the title is the outlier; a child who reads only the heading learns that nitrogen is something that gets repaired.

fact_en: Metallic character, the ability of an element to lose outer electrons and show luster and conductivity, increases as you move down a group and to the left across a period.
fact_bis: Ang metallic character, ang abilidad sa usa ka element nga mohatag og outer electrons ug magpakita og luster ug conductivity, motaas samtang mopaubos ka sa usa ka group ug pabaya sa usa ka period.

findings.note: "and to the left across a period" becomes "ug pabaya sa usa ka period". Cebuano pabaya = careless/negligent, not a direction; the corpus's word for "to the left" is pawala (dcard-06183 "patuo, pawala", ffct-22298, ffct-24137, ffct-24269, ffct-30260) and the same batch writes left side as "wala nga bahin" (dcard-10449). pabaya occurs exactly once in the whole sweep — here. A Cebuano-only reader gets "increases as you go down a group and [nonsense] across a period", so half the trend — the direction across a period — is unrecoverable from the card; nothing else on the card restores it.

fact_en: Before a volcanic eruption, prepare hard hats and masks to protect yourself from ash and falling debris.
fact_bis: Sa dili pa moubo ang bulkan, pag-andam ug hard hat ug mask aron protektahan ang kaugalingon sa abo ug matumba nga debris.

findings.note: EN "Before a volcanic eruption, prepare hard hats and masks" -> BIS "Sa dili pa moubo ang bulkan, pag-andam ug hard hat ug mask". Cebuano ubo = TO COUGH (corpus: 83 cards use ubo/mo-ubo for coughing, e.g. ffct-04474 'Kung mo-ubo o mobahin'); eruption is mobuto/mo-ulbo. The card never uses the correct verb anywhere, so the event the whole safety instruction is keyed to ('before the eruption') is named as the volcano coughing. Sibling cards in this same batch get it right (dcard-10794/10795 'pag-ulbo sa bulkan', dcard-10785 'niulbo'), and 'moubo ang bulkan' appears nowhere else in the 47k-card corpus.

fact_en: Know the evacuation plans and the location of the evacuation center in your community before a volcanic eruption.
fact_bis: Hibaloi ang mga evacuation plan ug lokasyon sa evacuation center sa inyong komunidad sa dili pa moubo ang bulkan.

findings.note: EN "before a volcanic eruption" -> BIS "sa dili pa moubo ang bulkan". Only 'abo'/'bulkan' context is absent here (the card is purely about evacuation plans), so nothing in the card restores the meaning of the misused verb; the child is told to learn evacuation plans 'before the volcano coughs'.

fact_en: Keep updated on unusual volcanic activity through TV, newspaper, or radio before an eruption.
fact_bis: Magpabiling updated sa lahi nga kalihokan sa bulkan pinaagi sa TV, mantalaan, o radyo sa dili pa kini moubo.

findings.note: EN "before an eruption" -> BIS "sa dili pa kini moubo". Weakest anchor of the five: no ash, lava or eruption noun anywhere in the card, so the eruption is referred to only by a pronoun plus a verb that means TO COUGH in Cebuano. Corpus check: 'moubo' otherwise only appears for coughing (ffct-02413) or falling pressure (ffct-35155).

fact_en: Wear protective clothing, headgear, and high-efficiency dust masks during a volcanic eruption to keep ash out of your lungs.
fact_bis: Pagsul-ob ug protective clothing, headgear, ug high-efficiency dust mask kon moubo ang bulkan aron dili makasulod ang abo sa baga.

findings.note: EN "during a volcanic eruption" -> BIS "kon moubo ang bulkan" = when the volcano COUGHS. Same wrong-sense verb; here it also shifts the timing the card depends on (this card is the DURING-eruption instruction, while dcard-10787/10789 are the BEFORE-eruption ones and use the identical 'moubo' phrasing), so a Cebuano-only child cannot tell the two apart. Correct word (pag-ulbo / mobuto) never appears in the card.

fact_en: Follow evacuation orders from authorities during a volcanic eruption and stay in the evacuation center until further instructions.
fact_bis: Sunda ang mga mando sa pagbakwit gikan sa mga awtoridad kon moubo ang bulkan ug pabilin sa evacuation center hangtod adunay dugang nga instruksyon.

findings.note: EN "Follow evacuation orders from authorities during a volcanic eruption" -> BIS "Sunda ang mga mando sa pagbakwit ... kon moubo ang bulkan". ubo = cough, not erupt; the card carries no other word for eruption (unlike dcard-10797 'Human sa pag-ulbo sa bulkan' in the same batch), so the trigger condition for evacuating is misnamed.
